title: Symmetry-Protected Pinch Curves in Classical Spin Liquids
abstract: Classical spin liquids are correlated paramagnets in which local constraints generate extensive degeneracy and emergent gauge structures, often observable as pinch-point singularities in spin structure factors. Here we introduce pinch-curve spin liquids, in which the pinch singularities form one-dimensional algebraic curves in momentum space. Inversion symmetry protects these curves by reducing the singularity condition to two real algebraic constraints in three dimensions, and the geometry of the pinch locus is algebraically programmable. We identify elementary mechanisms for generating straight and curved pinch loci, construct lattice spin models that realize them, and test the predicted structure factors using Monte Carlo simulations. We further show that pinch curves can host an infrared Gauss-law transition: the leading local constraint and the associated anisotropic scaling of the structure factor change, even though the singular locus remains one-dimensional.
summary: This work develops the theory of 'pinch-curve spin liquids,' where magnetic correlations exhibit singularities forming 1D curves in momentum space. By exploiting inversion symmetry, the constraints defining these curves are mathematically simplified and shown to be algebraically programmable. The research confirms that these systems undergo a novel Gauss-law transition while maintaining their singular geometric structure.
main_problem: The paper introduces 'pinch-curve spin liquids,' generalizing classical spin liquids where correlation singularities form one-dimensional algebraic curves in momentum space.
main_result: Symmetry protection reduces the singularity condition to two real polynomial constraints, allowing for algebraically programmable pinch loci that host an infrared Gauss-law transition.
method: The analysis combines continuum theory using polynomial constraint equations with lattice simulations (Monte Carlo) on spin models derived from generalized Gauss's laws.
model_or_system: Classical spin liquids are modeled by two-component scalar-charge Gauss's laws, leading to a Hamiltonian constrained by local operators in momentum space. The system is studied via its singular locus $\mathbf{Z}$ defined by the common zeros of these constraints.
key_observables: The structure factor $\langle S_{a}(\mathbf{k})S_{b}(-\mathbf{k})angle$ and the geometry of the pinch curve in momentum space ($\mathbf{k}$).
important_parameters: Inversion symmetry ($I$), lattice size ($L=50$), and the degree/homogeneity of the polynomial constraints.
main_assumptions: The analysis often focuses on diagonal symmetry cases, simplifying the constraint to $P_1(\mathbf{k}) = P_2(\mathbf{k}) = 0$.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate geometric intersections in k-space (straight vs. curved lines) and compare structure factors from lattice models against zero-mode predictions; one figure shows the transition of the local constraint order.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from defining pinch-curve spin liquids via symmetry protection, deriving algebraic constraints ($P_1=P_2=0$), classifying the geometry based on polynomial forms (homogeneous vs. inhomogeneous), and finally validating these predictions using lattice Monte Carlo simulations and analyzing phase transitions.
why_interesting: It provides a rigorous mathematical framework for understanding emergent topological features (singular loci) in classical spin systems, linking algebraic geometry directly to physical correlation functions.
